beats.text: For number fields, isomorphic Galois groups come from isomorphic fields
Uchida (1981) conjectured the same for open homomorphisms, not only isomorphisms
The claim: yes, for solvably closed extensions, with no restriction on the kernel

sources.quote: Neukirch-Uchida theorem (isomorphisms). Uchida (1981, 'Homomorphisms of Galois groups of solvably closed Galois extensions', J. Math. Soc. Japan) conjectured the homomorphism version and proved it when F1 = Q, uniqueness in general, and existence under a local condition.
every continuous open homomorphism Gal(E1/F1) -> Gal(E2/F2) is induced by a unique field embedding E2 -> E1; no restriction on the kernel.

plain: A number field's symmetry group remembers the field; even a one-way map of symmetries comes from fields

steps: Start from any open map between the two Galois groups
Show it respects roots of unity, from openness alone
Hoshi's criterion then gives the field embedding

boxes: an open map of Galois groups

voice.text: Isomorphic Galois groups come from isomorphic fields. Uchida asked the same for open maps.
Openness alone forces compatibility with roots of unity, and a known criterion finishes.
Claimed: every open map comes from fields.
